sections.content:
49,015 people

were counted on the census as "sales administrators" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Sales administrators provide support to the process of selling equipment, materials and other products or services.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "sales administrators" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "sales administrators", 14.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "sales administrators" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "sales administrators" included:

  • catering and bar managers
  • data entry administrators
  • legal associate professionals

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "sales administrators" there were more women than men (78% compared with 22%).

This means "sales administrators" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "administrative occupations".

Men made up 22% and women made up 78% of "sales administrators"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "sales administrators" included:

  • cleaners and domestics
  • welfare professionals (other)
  • visual merchandisers and related occupations

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "sales administrators" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged under 30 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "sales administrators" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "sales administrators", 9.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (70.5% compared with 29.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (92.8%) than self-employed (7.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
